Hvidovre (Hvidovre Hospital) is a major healthcare facility and university department in Denmark that plays a critical role in the national diagnostic framework for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). As part of the broader national effort tracked by the DANIBD database to standardize and improve IBD diagnostics, Hvidovre handles both adult and highly specialized pediatric cases.

In the 2024 DANIBD report evaluating national quality indicators, Hvidovre was identified as one of only four departments—alongside [[ouh-svendborg|OUH Svendborg]], [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]], and [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]]—that failed to meet the target for [[indikator-1a|Indikator 1a]] [^src1]. Specifically, these four departments achieved a fulfillment rate of under 70% for newly diagnosed adults being examined in accordance with clinical recommendations [^src1]. 

Beyond adult diagnostics, Hvidovre is one of the three largest university departments in the country, alongside Odense and Aarhus, responsible for the specialized diagnostics of the youngest children with [[veo-ibd|VEO-IBD]] (very-early onset IBD) [^src1]. This specialized pediatric mandate significantly influences the department's internal coding practices and its application of MRI scanning for its youngest patients, tying directly into national analyses regarding the use of small bowel MRIs in children.
